scope: Five maintained files plus generated gcc-cmake evidence and its private handwritten qualification harness; parent /root sole implementation writer

admission.scope: Tiny CMake fixture; sequential single-job builds only

static_review: The toolchain gates the native Darwin ARM64 host, gcc16 profile selection, normalized compiler prefix, selected inherited flags, existing compiler choices, absolute SDK with settings file, explicit deployment target format and arm64 architecture. The harness separately attests exact runtime/compiler/SDK/tool hashes.

The fixture uses Ninja Multi-Config, GNU C++ 16.2.0, C++26 without extensions, and target-private reflection/warning flags. The positive source is the already reviewed reflection witness; it introduces no install, dependency, service or cache-server action.

Generated compilation commands and per-configuration summaries identify the intended compiler, SDK, arm64 and deployment target. Optimization/debug flags correspond to Debug, Release, RelWithDebInfo and MinSizeRel.
CMake emits its native module-scanning flags for this source. The tested fixture uses ordinary includes; this review does not establish named-module or import-std acceptance.

Each configuration has a successful build, CTest result, independent direct runtime return code, ARM64 binary observation and exact loaded GCC libstdc++ image path. All four tested isolation failures stop with their intended diagnostics.

The harness runs sequentially with one build job, offline mise and inherited auto-install disabled. It records command return codes/log hashes, raises on unexpected results and terminates its owned process group on timeout/interruption; timeout injection was not repeated here.
README and selected plan limit completion to the tiny CMake fixture; vcpkg/application matrix/compiler-cache and broader toolchain work remain unqualified.
